Plot of the posterior density of a diagnostic

Source: R/plot-functionals.R
plot_functionals.Rd

Plots the exact posterior density of the informativeness, or of another diagnostic, with its posterior mean, its value at the posterior mean of sigma_tau^2 and its central posterior interval.

Usage

plot_functionals(
  x,
  which = c("I", "mean", "H", "J_eff", "sigma_tau"),
  level = NULL,
  plugin = TRUE,
  scale = 1,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

An object of class reliability_posterior or reliability_draws, or a profile_comparison of them.

which

The diagnostic: one of "I" (the default), "mean", "H", "J_eff" or "sigma_tau".

level

Probability content of the shaded interval, a number between 0 and 1. NULL, the default, uses the level of the fit.

plugin

If TRUE (the default), a dashed line marks the value at the posterior mean of sigma_tau^2, when that mean exists.

scale

Factor that multiplies sigma_tau for which = "sigma_tau", a positive number.

...

Must be empty.

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

For a posterior fit the density comes from functional_density(). The density of the informativeness grows without bound as \(I\) approaches 0 under every prior offered by sd_prior(), whereas the posterior density of sigma_tau has a finite positive limit at 0. For draws it is a kernel density estimate of the draws. For the informativeness, a label gives the posterior probability that \(I\) exceeds the threshold of the fit; the gray line is at one half, where the second-order term of the mean reliability minus \(I\) changes sign. See prob_above().

Examples

fit <- reliability_posterior(estimate, se = se, data = eight_schools)
plot_functionals(fit)

plot_functionals(fit, which = "H")
